lessons: C1-7: Exit on evidence, not price - CAT was rightly held through a -5% dip (C5) and rightly sold on margin deterioration (C7).
C8: Don't trim winners on sector-wide fear when the company is executing - AMZN popped +14.7% on earnings after being held through the AI-capex scare.
C10-11: A >5% same-day spike is a chase - CAT's earnings pop fully round-tripped within 3 trading days.
C10-12/C22/C25: Business quality and chart trend are separate signals; a beat on a broken chart (ORCL, RH, AZO) still fails.
C1-12: Diversification rules silently turned the book into an index fund - every dollar needs a specific why_not_voo.
C15-27: 12 no-trade cycles were an arithmetic deadlock (count band + cash band), not caution - if 'no trades' repeats 3+ cycles, audit the rules, don't re-flag the backlog.
C19->C27: Queued scores decay - MDT went 22/25 -> 17/25 while waiting. Re-score anything older than 2 cycles before buying.
C23-24: Holding through an intact-thesis drawdown can pay - the AI-safety selloff reversed within days; UNP drew a UBS upgrade while held.
C27: Fast runs cut corners - Cycle 27 took 37s, skipped its heartbeat, and its technicals call failed on missing params. Use the cheat-sheet; never skip steps 2/3/8/9.
Ops: always git fetch before judging state (stale-clone false alarm, 2026-08-05); required files can be silently gitignored (*.log, C11).
